issues.message: A bare OpenSpec change id still resolves to an unrelated plan when any plan basename contains it: Form 2 (substring) runs before Form 2c. Probed: openspec/changes/auth exists, plans/2026-11-01_feature_auth-refactor.md exists, `mb-work-resolve.sh auth` prints the plan path rc=0, no sync, no specs/ created. Realistic trigger: a wrapper plan named after the same change (…_feature_add-widget-cache.md) makes `/mb work add-widget-cache` skip the sync and the conflict stop, the same silent-replacement class as prior finding 1 and a breach of AGR-105 ('/mb work <change-id> syncs first, stops on conflict').
issues.fix: Check for an existing <project>/openspec/changes/<id> before the Form 2 substring search (or exit 2 as ambiguous when both a change and a plan match); add a bats case with a colliding plan basename.

issues.message: Form 3b row still says 'A native topic of the same name wins unless it carries openspec_source', the opposite of the fixed behaviour (native topic + same-named change now exits 1, as does a topic linked to a different change). The driver reads this table as the resolver contract; the resolver header comment (scripts/mb-work-resolve.sh:4-9) also omits the new form.
issues.fix: Replace the sentence with: a same-named native topic or a topic linked to another change exits 1 and suggests `mb-openspec.sh import <dir> --as <topic>`; add form 2c to the header list.

issues.message: The inline python re-implements slugify (mb_openspec_paths.slugify), frontmatter parsing (mb_openspec_bank.parse_frontmatter) and the linkage check (mb_openspec_ops._assert_linked_to). The parse at :300 (`read().split('---')[1:2]`) is looser than _FRONTMATTER_RE: in a file without frontmatter it reads the text between two body horizontal rules as frontmatter. Outcome is fail-closed today, but the two slug/link rules can drift apart.
issues.fix: Import slugify/parse_frontmatter/resolve_stored_source from the scripts dir in the helper instead of copying them.

issues.message: Mode copy duplicates mb_fs_atomic._target_mode and runs inside the rename loop: an exists()/stat() race or a chmod OSError after earlier os.replace calls aborts mid-batch, adding a failure point after the first rename (the partial-batch recovery itself is I-299, not re-raised). The prior recommendation was to reuse the established primitive.
issues.fix: Apply `os.chmod(tmp, _target_mode(dest))` in stage() right after writing the temp file, before any rename.
